# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

**Top pick: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900.** It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output and a 10 ms UPS switchover. It takes 800 W of solar input and accepts an add-on battery later, which the Bluetti Elite 200 V2 can't. One source estimates about 23 hours on a fridge, CPAP and router. [Buy via Outage Authority's roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup) (links to Amazon) or see it on [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/).

## Other good options

| Pick | Price | Capacity / output | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bluetti Elite 200 V2** | $899 on two sites, but see the note below | 2,074 Wh / 2,600 W | Rated for 6,000 cycles and has the most capacity of the group. It can't be expanded. |
| **Bluetti AC180** (budget) | $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF | 1,152 Wh / 1,800 W | The most watt-hours per dollar under $500, with a 5-year warranty. It runs the fridge, CPAP and router for about 13 hours. [Buy at Bluetti](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) |
| **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (lightest) | $489 at Outbound Power, $559 at Jackery | 1,070 Wh / 1,500 W | At 23.8 lb it's the easiest to carry, but it's only a one-night bridge (about 12 hours). Solar input is limited to 400 W. [Review and buy links](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2) |
| **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max** | $899 | 2,048 Wh / 2,400 W | A solid alternative to the Anker at the same price. [See the comparison](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/) |
| **Anker SOLIX F1500** (deal) | $599.99 | 1,536 Wh | Flagged as an unusually low price, and it's the cheapest per Wh among the larger units. I only have a price listing for it, so check reviews first. [Listing](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/) |

## Things to check before you buy
- **Elite 200 V2 pricing is inconsistent.** Outage Authority says Bluetti's own price returned to $1,199 after a promotion ended on Oct 7, though Amazon had it at $798.99 that day. Outage Outfitter and Compare Power Stations list $899. Confirm the price at checkout. At $900 or less it's a strong buy, but at $1,199 the Anker is the better one. [Source](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)
- **Match capacity to your outage.** A 1 kWh unit covers an overnight outage. For a multi-day outage or heavier loads like a window AC, choose a 2 kWh unit.
- **None of these will run a whole house.** They cover essentials like a fridge, internet, a CPAP and lights.
- **The review sites earn affiliate commissions**, and their specs come from the manufacturers rather than their own testing. Prices change often.
